title: Pakistan: Human Rights Organizations Call for Release of Political Prisoner Idris Khattak
content:
On the seven-year anniversary of Idris Khattak’s detention in Pakistan, we, the undersigned organizations, call for his immediate and unconditional release. 

Idris Khattak is a well-known Pashtun human rights defender who spent decades documenting human rights abuses, including enforced disappearances, in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province and the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas. On November 13, 2019, he was abducted and disappeared. For the next seven months, his family did not know whether he was alive or dead.

title: Defeating Authoritarian Digital Blackouts: Countering Internet Shutdowns Through Satellite Technology
content:
(Photo Credit: Diego Martinez / Alamy Live News.)

As mass antigovernment and economic protests erupted last winter across multiple Iranian cities, ordinary Iranians took to the streets to demand better living conditions. In response, the Iranian regime not only brutally murdered thousands in the streets but also shut off the internet to hide its crimes from the world and prevent its people from communicating with each other.

Fortunately, there is a way to counter this insidious digital oppression. Satellite internet provides a means for the Iranian people to circumvent the government’s internet shutdown, but Tehran is attempting to block satellite internet over its territory, branding it a “tool of war,” and is pressuring other governments and international bodies to restrict satellite services in the name of “digital sovereignty.”

Democratic governments, donors, and the satellite industry should take a stand to counter the Iranian regime’s attempt to ground the satellites providing the Iranian people a voice and a lifeline.

title: Freedom House Launches New US Democracy Tracker, Identifies Serious Concerns
content:
WASHINGTON—Freedom House, in partnership with the Charles F. Kettering Foundation, today launched the US Democracy Tracker, a new, quarterly assessment of democratic institutions and fundamental freedoms in the United States. The inaugural edition identifies government accountability and freedom of the media as areas of “serious concern.”

“Near record-high numbers of Americans just exercised their civic duty to vote in the midterm elections. Yet a robust democracy is defined not simply by elections, but by how our constitutional freedoms are protected in practice. Our new US Democracy Tracker offers a vital measure of the state of our freedoms at an important time in our democracy,” said Jamie Fly, CEO of Freedom House. 

Since 1973, Freedom House has assessed political rights and civil liberties in over 200 countries and territories. The US Democracy Tracker is derived from the same rigorous research methods to assess conditions crucial to democracy in the United States. It examines eight categories including free elections, political competition, accountability, access to justice, media freedom, and other fundamental rights.

title: Freedom House Announces Laura Rosenberger as Executive Vice President
content:
WASHINGTON—Freedom House today announced that Laura Rosenberger has joined the organization as executive vice president. A widely respected and experienced democracy, foreign policy, and national security leader, Rosenberger will work with Freedom House CEO Jamie Fly to guide the organization as it expands its research, programming, and advocacy efforts during a period of strategic growth.

“Laura has spent her career confronting authoritarianism and championing democracy,” said Fly. “It is an honor to welcome her to our leadership team. Our Freedom in the World report has found that today just 21 percent of the world’s people live in countries rated Free, down from 46 percent two decades ago. Laura’s deep policy experience and work strengthening democratic resilience will be invaluable as Freedom House fights to reverse democratic decline.”

title: Hong Kong: Human Rights Organizations Condemn Unjust Sentencing of Joshua Wong
content:
We, the undersigned organizations, condemn the November 5th sentencing of Hong Kong prodemocracy advocate Joshua Wong to a 10-year sentence by the Hong Kong High Court. This is the second time he has been sentenced under the Beijing-imposed National Security Law (NSL), which has contributed to the rapid deterioration of basic freedoms in Hong Kong.

Joshua, who marked his 30th birthday in prison three weeks ago, rose to prominence as a teenager as the cofounder of the student group Scholarism, which opposed the introduction of pro-Beijing propaganda into Hong Kong's schools. He helped lead the historic 2014 Umbrella Movement and in 2016 created the prodemocracy Demosistō party, which was forced to disband after the approval of the NSL in 2020. He has received international acclaim for his democratic activism, including multiple nominations for the Nobel Peace Prize.

title: The 2027 Mark Palmer Prize: Call for Nominations
content:
Freedom House is now accepting nominations for the 2027 Mark Palmer Prize, inviting individuals and organizations around the world to put forward candidates whose work exemplifies the important role of diplomacy in supporting democratic movements and defending fundamental freedoms.

The award takes its name from the late Mark Palmer, a longtime Freedom House trustee and US ambassador to Hungary from 1986 to 1990. In 1989, as the Cold War was coming to a close, Palmer boldly joined civil society and the Hungarian democratic opposition to support the country’s transition to democracy.
 
The Mark Palmer Prize has been awarded to diplomats and international civil servants from around the world, including Georgia, Peru, the Czech Republic, Lithuania, Mongolia, Sweden, Canada, Uruguay, and the United States. The prize is made possible through the generosity of the Mark and Sushma Palmer Legacy Fund, established by Dr. Sushma Palmer in loving memory of her late husband and former Freedom House trustee and vice chairman Ambassador Mark Palmer. 

Nomination Form

Criteria 

The award winner must be a current or former diplomat or official serving in an intergovernmental institution.

title: Nicaragua’s Future: Repression, Resistance, and Hope
content:
Register


Over the past two decades, Nicaragua has experienced one of the world's most dramatic declines in freedom, losing 49 points on Freedom in the World’s 100-point scale assessing political rights and civil liberties. The regime of Daniel Ortega and his wife and “co-president” Rosario Murillo has systematically dismantled democratic institutions, imprisoned political opponents, killed peaceful protestors, and shuttered thousands of civil society organizations, independent media outlets, and religious institutions. Moreover, it has exported its repression beyond Nicaragua's borders, targeting dissidents in neighboring Costa Rica with surveillance, intimidation, and violence. The regime has also deepened its cooperation with other authoritarian powers, including those ruling China, Cuba, Russia, and Iran.
